_source: docs/content-bible.md §7 (fixed rosters). Transcribed verbatim, never invented (G2). Roster sizes including the signature are 3 / 4 / 5 / 6 / 6 / 6 — asserted in tests/unit/transcription.test.ts and by core/schemas.ts GYM_ROSTER_SIZES.
_amendment: Authorised by Hank: Maribel's roster is THREE, not the bible's four. The duplicate Nibbin (A) slot was cut; she keeps Bramblehog (A), Skir (A) and the signature "Old Nib" Nibbin (E). Chosen by measurement, not taste — of the three possible cuts the harness put Nibbin (A) first on every axis. This amends bible §7 and build-doc Hard Req 9.
_schema: build-doc §7.7 ghost-compatible: every leader ships source:"fixed". "ghost" is schema-only (Hard Req 9); building any ghost feature is guardrail G8.
_levels: bible §7 gives no levels. Ramp assigned by rule: roster level = 8 + 6×(gym−1) → 8/14/20/26/32/38; the signature is +2 → 16/22/28/34/40, so the last signature sits exactly on the level cap 40 (build-doc §7.4). EXCEPTION, gym 1: Maribel's signature is +0, level 8. A flat +2 is a level premium that shrinks as a FRACTION of the player's level — 25% of a level-8 team, 5% of a level-38 one — so it lands hardest at the one gym the harness measured as the hardest in the game. Old Nib is still unambiguously the ace: an Elder — the bonus is `balance.age.multiplier.E`, ×1.075 today — with Thick Pelt (+10% def) against level-parity Adults. RE-CHECKED after the T-10 halving, on core/battle.ts effectiveStats and these shipped slots: at level 8 Old Nib totals 422 effective stats against 348 for BOTH Bramblehog (A) and Skir (A), and is 1.105× a same-line level-parity Adult. The margin narrowed (it was 450 vs 348 at ×1.15) but did not invert, so the +0 premium still stands. Its shape did change: Skir still outruns it (62 spd vs 99) and now all but matches its attack (82 vs 81, was 88 vs 81), so the claim now rests on bulk — 110 hp / 106 def against Skir's 64 / 58 — rather than on leading everywhere.
_lineIds: Juvenile line-forms are keyed by LINE id, not form name (build-doc §7.1): Bogling = mirefin-line age J, Gloomgrub = gloomoth-line age J.
_actNotYear: `act` WAS `year`, renamed on Hank's authorisation. It was never a calendar year — tools/harness/player.ts has always read it as 'how far along the player is' (`actNodeIds`) — but content-bible §6's 'Six acts = six years' equation made the two indistinguishable, and 44 dialogue entries were written against the wrong one. Under the amended L8 the calendar is unbounded and independent, so Odo is the act-2 leader whether the player reaches him in calendar year 2 or year 11. The field is named for the axis it is on so nobody re-conflates them. bible §7 labels the column 'Yr'; the numbers are unchanged.
_rival: content-bible §8 — 'Wick — a Cullbrand Company apprentice your age. Battles you each act. His philosophy is harvest-first; the routes he's worked are visibly degraded when you reach them. His team always includes Carricrow — he profits from collapse.' Only two of those clauses are content the bible STATES: he fights once per act, and Carricrow is always on the team. EVERY OTHER SLOT IS AUTHORED, NOT DERIVED, and it is authored under one machine-checkable rule so it cannot drift into invention: every slot's line lives on a route Wick has ALREADY WORKED (r1..rN), which is the bible's own 'the routes he's worked' clause read as a roster constraint. That reading is what makes the last fight fieldable at all — data/nodes/sanctum-approach.json carries carricrow-line and nothing else, so a team drawn from the act-6 node alone would be one animal. LEVELS are balance.encounter.levelByYear transcribed by ACT (6/12/18/24/30/36), i.e. the region's own wild band at that act, which puts every rival slot two levels under the act's leader (8/14/20/26/32/38); core/schemas.ts asserts that gap, because a rival who out-levels the badge that opens the next act inverts the ladder. His act-5 and act-6 Carricrow is an ELDER because his own act-5 line says so ('my Carricrow is an Elder now') — that slot is transcribed, not chosen. He is NOT a gyms[] row: game/gym-battle.ts keys leaders by `town` and winGym awards a badge, so a seventh leader standing on Route 1 would hand out a badge for beating the rival.
